Mage ArcaneMythic+S2026-08-09Season 2 PTR — M+ outlook (final pre-launch M+ tier list, ranked for the highest keys) · Top of S tier and his pick for best spec in the season: among the highest overall damage while also leading single-target boss damage, and it keeps full priority damage during AoE with some funnel on top. He reads the defensive complaints as outdated — two baseline Barrier charges, a Mirror Image stagger and extra avoidance make it durable enough to build around.Retained at cutoffReceipt source
Warrior ArmsMythic+S2026-08-09Season 2 PTR — M+ outlook (final pre-launch M+ tier list, ranked for the highest keys) · Second S-tier spec, which he flags as a surprise. Lower overall than the big AoE specs but single-target priority damage on par with Arcane, and unusually strong on two-to-three target cleave, which he says several dungeons in the pool reward for long stretches. Caveat: it is on Slayer now, which he rates weaker than Colossus. He expects nearly every comp to run Arcane or Arms, often both.Retained at cutoffReceipt source
Demon Hunter DevourerMythic+A+2026-08-09Season 2 PTR — M+ outlook (final pre-launch M+ tier list, ranked for the highest keys) · Top of A+. Strong damage with two builds — Annihilator for AoE with low single target, Voidguard for single target with moderate AoE — plus Chaos Brand, Darkness and genuine tankiness, which he argues is undervalued after watching DK/DH survive content others could not in Season 1. He calls it the most likely spec to round out a group; the caveats are having to commit to one build and very high sims that could invite a raid-driven nerf.Retained at cutoffReceipt source
Shaman ElementalMythic+A2026-08-09Season 2 PTR — M+ outlook (final pre-launch M+ tier list, ranked for the highest keys) · A tier. Very good sustained five-target damage, now a consistent rather than bursty spec, decent single target and workable two-to-three target on the Farseer build, plus Skyfury as a group buff. Held out of S only because he thinks several comparable specs exist, and because stacking it with other squishy specs worries him defensively. He notes all mail specs are roughly 3% inflated on PTR by a mail-only bug.Retained at cutoffReceipt source
Druid BalanceMythic+Unknown2026-08-09Season 2 PTR — M+ outlook (final pre-launch M+ tier list, ranked for the highest keys) · He rates it similar to Elemental Shaman — a big AoE spec with weaker single target and no priority damage during AoE — and provides Mark of the Wild, which has never been dropped in past seasons. But he pushes back on the assumption that a Druid is auto-included: he considers Elemental a slightly better version of the same role, and thinks a no-Mark season is genuinely possible. · No unambiguous absolute placement preserved in this video paraphraseRetained at cutoffReceipt source
Death Knight UnholyMythic+A+2026-08-09Season 2 PTR — M+ outlook (final pre-launch M+ tier list, ranked for the highest keys) · A+. He argues the DKs were written off after an early-PTR nerf and are still good, pointing to Unholy logs topping overall damage with strong AoE and priority damage. The stated weakness is low single target. He notes it can operate at full range, unlike Frost.Retained at cutoffReceipt source
Death Knight FrostMythic+A+2026-08-09Season 2 PTR — M+ outlook (final pre-launch M+ tier list, ranked for the highest keys) · A+ alongside Unholy, with a damage profile he rates somewhat worse — rampy this season and more reliant on Skyfury, so he would want a Shaman in the group or would play Unholy instead. He also argues a DPS DK alongside a Blood DK is viable because the overlapping utility is mostly personal.Retained at cutoffReceipt source
Rogue SubtletyMythic+A-2026-08-09Season 2 PTR — M+ outlook (final pre-launch M+ tier list, ranked for the highest keys) · A- and, he says, a real contender: currently carrying a positive bug worth roughly 5% too much damage, but strong on both AoE and single target even after discounting that. His caveat is stability rather than ceiling — he calls it historically the most bug-prone spec and expects it to be a nerf candidate.Retained at cutoffReceipt source
Rogue OutlawMythic+A-2026-08-09Season 2 PTR — M+ outlook (final pre-launch M+ tier list, ranked for the highest keys) · A-. Lots of AoE and strong single target, but more dependent on a specific pull style than the other Rogue specs. He thinks target cap is not very relevant this season given few large uncapped pulls, and that the buffs Outlaw wants will likely be present anyway given how good Warriors and Shamans look.Retained at cutoffReceipt source
Rogue AssassinationMythic+A-2026-08-09Season 2 PTR — M+ outlook (final pre-launch M+ tier list, ranked for the highest keys) · A- and his "dark horse" pick — few players on PTR since a recent buff, but the logs that exist show high overall and very good priority damage. Monk WindwalkerMythic+A-2026-08-09Season 2 PTR — M+ outlook (final pre-launch M+ tier list, ranked for the highest keys) · A-, slotted between Outlaw and Assassination. Shaman EnhancementMythic+B2026-08-09Season 2 PTR — M+ outlook (final pre-launch M+ tier list, ranked for the highest keys) · Top of B. Paladin RetributionMythic+B2026-08-09Season 2 PTR — M+ outlook (final pre-launch M+ tier list, ranked for the highest keys) · B tier and, in his words, the perpetual pug spec: good damage that is never quite enough to be best. Paladin HolyMythic+S2026-08-0112.1 PTR — Season 2 M+ healer tier list · Jak's only S-tier healer. He credits the raw output: the tier set turns Holy Light into an Infusion of Light engine (Inflorescence granting two, Judgment a 20% chance) and the 2-set doubles the healing of those Infusion-empowered Flash of Lights, while Virtue spell-queuing and Shield of the Righteous keep mana workable. He notes the post-buff Holy Shock means it is no longer a no-Shock build, and that the poison-dispel-heavy dungeon pool (six of eight) plus bleeds make Cleanse Toxins and Blessing of Protection unusually valuable. His own caveat: no raid buff and low personal damage, so if another healer is tuned to comparable output while bringing Skyfury or Mark of the Wild, Paladin can fall off the list.Retained at cutoffReceipt source
Shaman RestorationMythic+A2026-08-0112.1 PTR — Season 2 M+ healer tier list · A tier, and the top of it. Despite the Farseer buffs he still finds Totemic better in most dungeons — Farseer's single-target healing is good but the niche rarely gets realised when AoE healing is what the pull demands. He likes the tier set's extra Healing Rains stacking with Downpour and Acid Rain, especially in melee comps where everyone is inside them, but rates the raw output clearly below Holy Paladin (good AoE, weak single target) and calls the gameplay unexciting with no new resource or Apex interaction. Skyfury and Poison Cleansing Totem are what keep it high.Retained at cutoffReceipt source
Monk MistweaverMythic+Unknown2026-08-0112.1 PTR — Season 2 M+ healer tier list · He argues the attempt to force mastery into a good position broke the spec: buffing mastery while nerfing the Forecaster-side caster healing made the Rising Sun Kick / Ancient Teachings build dominant, and then the ~60% Morning Breeze cut removed it without restoring the rest. Conduit and Revival no longer feel like real cooldowns; Chi-Ji and Thunder Focus Tea still work but are much weaker; and the Season 1 backstop of falling back on casted healing does not function any more. His conclusion is blunt for a spec that was recently top of the list: Mistweaver actually needs buffs to get back to a good position. · No unambiguous absolute placement preserved in this video paraphraseRetained at cutoffReceipt source
Priest DisciplineMythic+B2026-08-0112.1 PTR — Season 2 M+ healer tier list · B tier. Output with the Oracle setup is fine — permanent Shadow Mend access, Surge of Light discounts and Divine Aegis absorbs off crits make it reliable — but Voidweaver is too weak, and the season's biggest problem is the dispel profile: with poisons in six of eight dungeons, a group that cannot cover the dispels eats through Pain Suppression charges. Mana is better than Season 1 but still has no active regeneration (even Shadowfiend barely helps), so drinking stops are unavoidable.Superseded at cutoffReceipt source
Priest HolyMythic+C2026-08-0112.1 PTR — Season 2 M+ healer tier list · C tier. He rates Oracle considerably stronger than Archon right now and says the healing output itself is genuinely good, but the spec is dragged down by cooldowns that do not feel strong (Prayer of Healing goes on the back burner without Archon's modifiers), heavy immobility, and weak Prayer of Mending. The revamped Apex turning every Serenity into a Benediction Flash Heal helps single-target but leaves it with no tool to lift the whole party at once. He credits a real niche — one of the strongest healers into rot damage — while concluding other healers are simply too well-rounded to pass up.Superseded at cutoffReceipt source
Druid RestorationMythic+C2026-08-0112.1 PTR — Season 2 M+ healer tier list · C tier, and his harshest read of the list. He accepts the Tranquility quality-of-life change but says everything else made the spec worse: losing the Swiftmend HoT extension and Burden of Vision leaves the HoTs feeling inert, the shift onto Clearcasting Regrowth does not compensate, and the granular control that made Resto Druid satisfying in dungeons is gone. Mastery no longer feels powerful, and outside Convoke or a trinket he does not see the output meeting the season's heal checks. He notes he has never seen Druid players this unhappy with the spec, and quotes one on stream to that effect.Retained at cutoffReceipt source
Evoker PreservationMythic+Unknown2026-08-0112.1 PTR — Season 2 M+ healer tier list · He rates the healing side as fully covered — the 2-set fires a Living Flame on Essence Burst consumption, the 4-set guarantees Essence Burst off Verdant Embrace, and Flame Shaper is strong with Dream Breath HoTs plus Fluttering Seedlings triggering Consume Flame — and he is seeing 90-100k personal damage in dungeons off double Fire Breath charges. What drags it down the list is unchanged: a proactive setup cost, far more GCDs and cognitive load than other healers, and an almost non-existent raid cooldown. His framing is that Preservation mains can meet the hardest HPS checks, but the extra work buys no extra reward over an easier healer. · No unambiguous absolute placement preserved in this video paraphraseRetained at cutoffReceipt source

Evoker PreservationRaidA2026-08-0412.1 PTR — Season 2 RAID healer tier list (Dummy Dome group testing) · A tier. Pres "blasted tons of healing" in the testing, with the Flameshaper setup putting better emphasis on Dream Breath and Consume Flame working with both fluttering seedlings and Verdant Embrace. It looked best when the raid was hard-stacked but still did a fantastic job on a light spread, and its mana economy read as being in a good spot. He cites UT's hands-on impression of being flooded with Essence Burst procs and going well over a million HPS inside a Stasis window.Retained at cutoffReceipt source
Paladin HolyRaidA2026-08-0412.1 PTR — Season 2 RAID healer tier list (Dummy Dome group testing) · A tier. He argues an underrated effect of the PTR's ~30% health-pool inflation is that Holy Light and Lay on Hands are no longer overweight, so the whole kit is appropriately sized to the new health bars. Output was "incredibly, incredibly high", especially on-demand spot healing. Caveat from Clarius after testing: it feels really strong when overhealing is low, hard to get value out of Virtue when other healers snipe it, and mana is a bit tight (though that should ease on a real fight where Virtue is not pressed on cooldown). He is unsure which Paladin spec ends up the race-to-world-first pick.Retained at cutoffReceipt source
Shaman RestorationRaidB2026-08-0412.1 PTR — Season 2 RAID healer tier list (Dummy Dome group testing) · B tier and the only spec there — he calls Resto Shaman the dark horse, "a tier away" from the world-first conversation. Strong when the raid can stack, and he flags Coiled Altar as a fight that should suit it (pulsing AoE plus stacking healing absorbs). The blocker is comp value rather than throughput: Harik's read, which he endorses, is that the numbers are genuinely good and mana is workable, but there is no reason to bring a Shaman as the fourth healer over a second Disc Priest unless you specifically want the Skyfury buff. One healer nerf above it would move it.Superseded at cutoffReceipt source
Priest HolyRaidC2026-08-0412.1 PTR — Season 2 RAID healer tier list (Dummy Dome group testing) · C tier. He tried both Oracle and Archon and says Holy Priest simply needs its passive healing to be stronger to succeed. Oracle should be favoured by a raid full of ticking rot damage and Prompt Prophecy buffs, but it was not — Archon was still stronger and is enormously bursty (Halo plus Apotheosis smashes health bars), while the gaps between cooldowns are boring and mana-starved. Every single test run ended near or at zero mana. His diagnosis: Blizzard keeps cutting Flash Heal and Prayer of Healing mana costs while removing the free casts (Surge of Light, Apotheosis Holy Words), so full-price casting still drains the bar.Superseded at cutoffReceipt source
Monk MistweaverRaidC2026-08-0412.1 PTR — Season 2 RAID healer tier list (Dummy Dome group testing) · C tier. Meg tested mastery-heavy Ancient Teachings and caster Mistweaver variants across multiple cooldown and comp setups and Mistweaver struggled throughout — not out of mana, but not producing much healing either. Her read, which he presents: the caster spells do nothing, the 8% aura nerf was unneeded given the state of the other healers, and Ancient Teachings only looks better because it is damage-based and therefore untouched by the healing-aura nerf. Her conclusion is that you would not bring a Monk in any competitive situation right now.Retained at cutoffReceipt source
Druid RestorationRaidUnknown2026-08-0412.1 PTR — Season 2 RAID healer tier list (Dummy Dome group testing) · Bottom of the list. He says Resto Druid has been struggling through all of Season 2 PTR testing and that the quality-of-life additions have left the spec feeling worse overall. Even in the environment that should suit it — stacked raid, constant rot and ticking damage — it consistently landed at the bottom of the group's raw output, with the testing splitting into a clear winners group and losers group. Viteman's asks, which he relays: buff HoTs, rework the 4-piece (the old one that granted Clearcasting synergised better), and rebuff Regrowth. · No unambiguous absolute placement preserved in this video paraphraseRetained at cutoffReceipt source

Monk MistweaverMythic+A2026-07-2812.1 PTR — Season 2 M+ testing · Drops Mistweaver to A tier in his retested M+ list. The mastery-stacking Morning Breeze / Rising Sun Kick build he had been calling S+ (Mistweavers doing 90–100k damage in keys with the healing to match) is dead after Morning Breeze effectiveness was cut 60%, on top of the ~8% overall healing nerf. Back on a normal stat priority it still felt quite strong on both damage and healing, but he calls the Sheilun/Vivify part of the toolkit weak and expects Blizzard to revisit it — which is why he no longer puts it in S.Superseded at cutoffReceipt source
Paladin HolyMythic+A2026-07-2812.1 PTR — Season 2 M+ testing · His biggest riser: high A tier, and he says some people would put it in S. Holy Shock healing +50% and its cheaper mana finally killed the no-Holy-Shock build, and the 4-set now carries what he thinks may be the first outright negative tier-set clause (Holy Light mana cost +60% in the notes, closer to 50% datamined) offset by a 5% healing increase. He reads that trade as good: you save Holy Light for emergencies and always have a button, and the spec's gameplay is simply better for it. Lightsmith with Beacon of Virtue pleasantly surprised him and he thinks he had been sleeping on it. Stays A only out of cautious optimism.Superseded at cutoffReceipt source
Shaman RestorationMythic+A2026-07-2812.1 PTR — Season 2 M+ testing · Keeps Resto Shaman where it was (A tier) and says he could nitpick it into S. Farseer's Chain Heal buffs made that tree feel decent, but Totemic in a full physical-melee composition felt really great, and he would be surprised if Totemic Resto is not part of that comp in Season 2.Superseded at cutoffReceipt source

But he separates that from the meta question and answers it himself: probably not meta, because it is harder to pilot, has range limitations and no good raid buff. Held at its existing placement. · No unambiguous absolute placement preserved in this video paraphraseSuperseded at cutoffReceipt source
Priest DisciplineMythic+B+2026-07-2812.1 PTR — Season 2 M+ testing · The healer that falls in this update — down to a new B+ row, because he admits he was generous in last week's ranking before testing most of the builds. A week focused on Oracle left mana still an issue and, more importantly, he wants more Atonement transfer in the panic moments: every healer above Discipline gave him an easier time in the same keys. He thinks a couple more tuning passes could make it climb, and that Blizzard is nervous about tuning it for M+ without breaking raid.Superseded at cutoffReceipt source
Druid RestorationMythic+Unknown2026-07-2812.1 PTR — Season 2 M+ testing · Held in place. The Abundance / Regrowth buffs and the Abundance crit bug fix landed, but he still wants further M+ buffs, and calls Wildstalker Resto's damage quite low — partly because there is no time to apply bleeds when the healing demand is that high. He also misses Verdant Infusion no longer extending HoTs and says he is jealous of the HoT-extension talent Resto Shaman just got. Expects Blizzard to keep buffing it, but flags that as speculation. · No unambiguous absolute placement preserved in this video paraphraseSuperseded at cutoffReceipt source
Priest HolyMythic+B2026-07-2812.1 PTR — Season 2 M+ testing · Stays around B tier. He is clear that Holy Priest is not bad and can push decently high keys, and the Oracle buffs (Premonition of Insight, Prayer of Mending) landed, but the currently popular dual-Oracle build leaves him with few healing buttons for his taste, its damage sits on the low end, and he wants significant — including gameplay — changes he is not holding his breath for.Superseded at cutoffReceipt source

Warlock DemonologyMythic+12026-07-2712.1 PTR — Season 2 M+ build dummy testing · Kalamazi's own M+-build dummy tests put Demonology ahead of the other two locks: roughly 130k sustained single target versus Affliction's ~110k, with near-identical baseline AoE (~380k) that climbs to 410-420k in Tyrant/implosion windows — the biggest cooldown swing of the three. He says the 20% Diabolist pet nerf still left the spec's Ruination, big-imp and axe-demon damage intact, and that "demo's not OP, it's just like aff is that bad". His ranking for 12.1 Mythic+ if it launched today: Demonology, then Affliction, then Destruction.Superseded at cutoffReceipt source
Warlock AfflictionMythic+22026-07-2712.1 PTR — Season 2 M+ build dummy testing · Kalamazi measures Affliction's M+-build single target at ~110k and calls the sustain outside cooldowns "abysmal … diabolically bad", pinning it on Unstable Affliction being undertuned — he wants roughly a 30% UA buff, which would also lift the tier set since it scales off baseline UA. AoE holds up at ~380k on Seed spam, and he credits the apex-talent and Dark Harvest bug fixes for a small AoE gain, but the Nocturnal Yield removal means Nightfall procs no longer give free instant Seeds, so shard economy and Agony upkeep now genuinely constrain the rotation. He ranks it second of the three for keys and says a UA buff is all it needs to be the pick.Retained at cutoffReceipt source
Warlock DestructionMythic+32026-07-2712.1 PTR — Season 2 M+ build dummy testing · Kalamazi still calls Destruction "our highest tuned spec currently in single target" — about 120k in his M+-build test, and steady rather than spiky — but adds that all three lock specs are subpar in single target versus other classes. In AoE it lands around 360-370k and is the hardest of the three to actually reach, because Mayhem keeps proccing on the main target or on low-health mobs; he says players have asked for two years to have Mayhem skip the primary target. He ranks it third of the three for 12.1 Mythic+ and describes the gameplay as sustaining one number rather than anything engaging.Superseded at cutoffReceipt source

Ordering within each role

Higher is better for all ranking measures. A dash means insufficient evidence or an unavailable comparison. Top-k selects 5 DPS or 3 tanks/healers; whole-group overlap is uninformative, while NDCG and rank correlation can still distinguish ordering.

Grading method 2: tied scores share their places at the cutoff, so overlap may be fractional. Ranking quality averages equally placed ties; spec names never break a scoring tie.
